
```{r}
grid_proportion_data <- read.csv("D:/UA_stuff/seagate_hard_drive/Nav Stress Data/nav_grid_proportion_byID.csv")
```

Extra analyses

Do people who learned the path better have different patterns of inner, outer, or novel grid usage?
```{r}
# To address the question, make a table with one row representing each person's adjusted percent correct and each type of grid proportion, collapsed across all conditions at first and noly with recreated path 1 since that is the one that happened before any stressors

recreate_avg <- recreate_data %>%
  group_by(subjectID) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_adj_percentCorrect = mean(adj_percent_correct))

grid_avg <- grid_proportion_data %>%
  group_by(subjectID, grid_type) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_grid_prop = mean(mean_grid_prop)
  )

recreate_grid_avg <- recreate_avg %>%
  left_join(grid_avg, by = "subjectID")

# Restructure the data
recreate_grid_avg$subjectID <- as.factor(recreate_grid_avg$subjectID)
recreate_grid_avg$grid_type <- as.factor(recreate_grid_avg$grid_type)

# Cool new graph! As average recreation percent increases, use of inner grid proportion increases (visually, stats next)
ggplot(recreate_grid_avg, 
       aes(x = avg_adj_percentCorrect, 
           y = avg_grid_prop,
           color = grid_type)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Average Recreation Percent Correct",
    y = "Grid Proportion",
    color = "Grid Type"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

# We will use an isometric log-ratio (ILR) transformation
# First, make the data wide to do the analysis

recreate_wide <- recreate_grid_avg %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = grid_type, values_from = avg_grid_prop)

# Check for proportions of zero
recreate_wide %>%
  summarise(
    inner_zero = sum(inner_proportion == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    outer_zero = sum(outer_proportion == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    novel_zero = sum(novel_proportion == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Calculate ILR coordinates
recreate_wide <- recreate_wide %>%
  mutate(
    ilr1 = sqrt(2/3) * log(
      inner_proportion / sqrt(outer_proportion * novel_proportion)
    ),
    ilr2 = sqrt(1/2) * log(
      outer_proportion / novel_proportion
    )
  )

# Run the regression model
grid_model <- manova(
  cbind(ilr1, ilr2) ~ avg_adj_percentCorrect,
  data = recreate_wide
)

summary(grid_model, test = "Pillai")

summary.aov(grid_model) # examine each separately

# So this analysis says that greater accuracy predicts using more inner grids
```

I am making a histogram of the navigation duration times to see how long people tended to take to navigate to an object
```{r}
hist(navTrials_data$Navigate_duration)

# Make a table of navigation block time for each person
block_duration <- navTrials_data %>%
  group_by(subjectID, block) %>%
  summarise(
    total_duration_s = sum(Navigate_duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_duration_min = total_duration_s/60,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Make a table of each person's total navigation test phase duration
navTest_duration <- navTrials_data %>%
  group_by(subjectID) %>%
  summarise(
    total_test_duration_s = sum(Navigate_duration, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_test_duration_min = total_test_duration_s/60
  )

# Range, mean, and sd duration for blocks and total test phase
range(block_duration$total_duration_min) # 11.3182 121.0454 (2hrs)
mean(block_duration$total_duration_min) # 31.76658
sd(block_duration$total_duration_min) # 20.82095

range(navTest_duration$total_test_duration_min) # 47.38689 244.52988 (4hrs)
mean(navTest_duration$total_test_duration_min) # 95.29975
sd(navTest_duration$total_test_duration_min) # 49.01016

```
